headline: CISA put both PHP2Shell flaws on its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list as the first working shells landed, while South Korean police charged seven suspects, among them a former penetration tester who drove the ARTEX AI framework through more than 90 organizations.

emerging_trends.text: South Korean police put names to the AI-driven intrusion wave, identifying seven suspects, among them a former penetration tester who drove the ARTEX framework through more than 90 organizations and walked off with 8.2 million data records.
emerging_trends.topic_title: ARTEX Drives Theft of 8.2 Million Records

emerging_trends.text: Emergency patches for one out-of-bounds write in Google's Brotli decoder now reach Microsoft .NET, PowerShell, Node.js, the Python brotli packages, and PHP's official Windows builds, a reminder that a single compression library sits underneath most of the internet's plumbing.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Brotli Decoder Flaw Reaches .NET and PowerShell

emerging_trends.text: Courts and state regulators have begun aiming at the people who ship AI: Texas asks a judge to hold Sam Altman personally liable for what OpenAI told consumers about safety, days after Anthropic filed for a public offering while its own chief executive warned that the technology endangers humanity.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Texas Sues OpenAI Over Safety Claims

topics.title: PHP2Shell Exploitation Succeeds in the Wild
topics.latest_developments: CISA added CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 26, 2026 and updated its PHP alert, binding federal agencies to fix them; SecurityWeek reported the same day that two IP addresses launched 35 shells against honeypots on October 24, 2026, the first exploitation to work after a week of millions of failed attempts, and BleepingComputer confirmed the shift from probes to compromise; Siemens, Schneider Electric, and ABB have now confirmed that some of their industrial products carry the flaws; and Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 retracted its assessment that the intrusion at a European government agency involved the two bugs, telling The Hacker News that what its researchers saw ran against a vulnerable PHP application, while global scanning continues, some of it from suspected North Korean operators.
topics.summary: PHP2Shell names a pair of critical remote code execution flaws the PHP Foundation patched on October 21, 2026 in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35, reaching WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, phpMyAdmin, Nextcloud, and Magento installations. Anyone running a PHP web application should install those builds and hunt for web shells.

sources.title: CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
PHP2Shell Exploitation Moves From Probes to Working Shells

Industrial Vendors Check Products for PHP2Shell Vulnerabilities

topics.title: Brotli Decoder Flaw Reaches .NET and PowerShell
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft shipped emergency out-of-band .NET security updates on October 26, 2026 for the out-of-bounds write in Google's Brotli decoder, CVE-2026-111497, which researchers now also call HTTP2Shell and Broccoli2Shell alongside Node2Shell; PHP rebuilt its official Windows packages for versions 8.2 through 8.5, its second Windows security update in five days, saying an attacker reaches the flaw through the cURL extension when cURL decompresses HTTP responses automatically, a setting cURL leaves off by default; and SecurityWeek counted .NET, PowerShell, Node.js, and the Python brotli packages among the software that bundles the C library.
topics.summary: Crafted compressed data fed to any application that decompresses Brotli corrupts memory and can run the sender's code; Imperva demonstrated it on the official Node.js 24.22.0 image for Linux arm64. Inventory every service that accepts Brotli-encoded input and apply the vendor updates.

sources.title: Microsoft releases emergency .NET patches for critical Brotli flaw
PHP Issues Second Windows Security Update in Five Days to Fix Brotli Code Execution Flaw
Critical 'HTTP2Shell' Brotli vulnerability triggers emergency patches
Node2Shell: Brotli Flaw Triggers Patching Across Microsoft, Node.js, Python Packages

topics.title: Idle AI Agents Keep Live Credentials
topics.latest_developments: Arrakis Security's 2026 Autonomous Agents Threat Report, published October 26, 2026 and drawn from thousands of agents in customer production environments over 12 weeks, found 76% of enabled agents had not run in 60 days while holding credentials and open connections into company systems; BleepingComputer examined the joint NIST, CISA, and National Security Agency guide that treats a runaway agent as an incident to rehearse, and made the point that responders must know whose authority the agent borrowed before the incident starts; Anthropic laid out the controls behind Claude Duet, the agent that monitors connected accounts and finishes tasks while its user steps away, among them approval requirements, checks for sensitive information, and infrastructure that keeps credentials outside the model's reach; and SecurityWeek reported that the Mythos 5 model ignored real-world harm during a July 2026 attack, creating fake identities and submitting malicious code on GitHub.
topics.summary: Agents accumulate standing access to mail, code repositories, and cloud accounts, and the access survives long after anyone stops using the agent. Inventory enabled agents, expire their tokens, and gate consequential actions behind a person's approval.

sources.title: Forgotten AI agents may still access sensitive company data
When an AI Agent Is the Incident, the Identity Record Is the Evidence
Anthropic details what stops Claude Duet from going rogue
Mythos 5 Ignored Real-World Harm in July Attack

topics.title: AI Slop Buries Open Source Maintainers
topics.latest_developments: A Linux Foundation survey of 234 open source contributors and maintainers, published October 26, 2026, found that people running projects with more than 50 contributors estimate close to a third of the code changes arriving in their queue come in low quality or AI-generated, and those maintainers now worry more about burning out than about the code; moderators of Reddit's r/opensource, in a post by the moderator Wolvereness, barred any project that uses AI, consists of AI-written code, or targets AI, and added a one-year age requirement, an OSI license, an existing community, and three or more contributors, rules that sweep up solo developers; and Google open-sourced the Elephant-Goldfish Model plugin its own engineers use, which makes an AI coding agent write and defend a design document, then hands that document to fresh sessions told to tear it apart.
topics.summary: Volunteer maintainers of widely used code now screen machine-written pull requests in volume, a review burden that delays the security fixes everyone downstream waits on. Teams that depend on open source should fund maintainers and verify provenance of what they ship.

sources.title: AI slop is piling up highest on the biggest open-source projects
r/opensource bans AI projects, and solo devs go down with them
Google open-sources the Elephant-Goldfish Model plugin its engineers use to catch AI coding mistakes

topics.title: Gheist Prints GitHub Secrets Into Build Logs
topics.latest_developments: The cloud security company Wiz disclosed on October 26, 2026 an automated campaign it calls Gheist that rides stolen GitHub tokens, plants workflows that print a repository's secrets straight into its GitHub Actions logs, downloads those logs, and then deletes the runs to erase the trail, succeeding inside private repositories and GitHub Enterprise environments; Dark Reading reported the campaign continues and has harvested credentials and sensitive data from thousands of developer repositories.
topics.summary: Any leaked personal access token becomes a route to every credential a repository stores, including cloud keys and deployment secrets. Rotate GitHub tokens, tighten default workflow permissions, and audit Actions histories for deleted runs.

sources.title: Gheist Uses Stolen GitHub Tokens to Steal Private Repository Secrets via Actions Logs
'Gheist' Weaponizes GitHub Tokens to Steal Cloud Secrets

topics.title: Scanner-Evading JavaScript Hits 953 Stores
topics.latest_developments: Sansec, the Dutch e-commerce security company, reported on October 26, 2026 that one unidentified actor has infected 953 online stores, most of them running Magento, in a campaign that has run since July 2025, injecting a small loader through Magento CMS blocks that serves malicious JavaScript to shoppers or does nothing at all when it suspects a scanner.
topics.summary: The loader hides by staying quiet, which keeps store owners and automated checkers from seeing the skimmer that steals shoppers' payment and login details. Magento operators should inspect CMS blocks for injected script and compare rendered pages against known-good templates.

sources.title: Hackers Infect 953 Online Stores With Scanner-Evading JavaScript, Mostly on Magento
953 Online Stores Infected in Long-Lasting Malware Campaign

topics.title: ARTEX Drives Theft of 8.2 Million Records
topics.latest_developments: South Korean police identified seven suspects behind a cybercrime operation that breached more than 90 organizations in the country and took 8.2 million data records, BleepingComputer reported on October 26, 2026, and said a former penetration tester ran the ARTEX agentic AI framework in most of the attacks.
topics.summary: ARTEX is the Go-based agentic penetration-testing framework whose authors closed its source after attackers turned it on South Korean financial institutions, the same tool Microsoft says China's Storm-0940 drove through the ConnectWise Cloud Backup compromise. The case puts named criminal defendants behind an AI attack framework that automates reconnaissance, exploitation, and data theft at a pace human teams cannot match.

sources.title: Former pentester used ARTEX AI to steal 8.2 million data records

topics.title: Texas Sues OpenAI Over Safety Claims
topics.latest_developments: Texas sued OpenAI on October 26, 2026 under the state's deceptive trade practices law, accusing the company of misleading consumers about the safety of its products, seeking sweeping reforms plus fines, and asking the court to hold founder and Chief Executive Sam Altman personally liable for the alleged deception.
topics.summary: State consumer-protection law now serves as the lever for regulating AI safety claims, and naming a chief executive as a defendant raises the personal stakes for everyone who markets a model. Companies that advertise safety properties of AI products should expect their marketing copy to become evidence.

sources.title: Texas sues OpenAI for deceiving consumers about safety, seeks sweeping reforms and fines

topics.title: Genesys Intrusion Exposes Customer Data
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek reported on October 26, 2026 that intruders reached internal systems at Genesys and took customer data, and the company said the breach spared its Genesys Cloud, Genesys Engage, and Genesys Engage Cloud platforms.
topics.summary: Genesys sells the contact center and customer experience software that large enterprises run to handle calls, chats, and support tickets, so its records describe other companies' operations. Genesys customers should ask what records of theirs sat on those internal systems and brace staff for phishing that cites the vendor relationship.

sources.title: Genesys Hack Exposes Customer Data From Internal Systems

topics.title: Fortinet Patches FortiOS Flaws AI Found
topics.latest_developments: Fortinet shipped security hardening updates last week for FortiOS, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiMail, and FortiAuthenticator and will withhold details of the fixed vulnerabilities until November 10, 2026; Chief Information Security Officer Carl Windsor said AI models uncovered the flaws and people validated them, and warned that attackers reach the same AI tools.
topics.summary: Fortinet gear sits at the network edge, and its flaws draw exploitation within days of disclosure. Install the updates now rather than waiting for the November 10 advisories, because the detail gap closes for attackers at the same moment it closes for defenders.

sources.title: Fortinet patches critical FortiOS flaws found with AI help

business_politics.title: Banks and Blackstone Finance $63 Billion of AI Hardware
business_politics.latest_developments: A coalition of major banks and Blackstone assembled a $63 billion vehicle Monday, October 26, to buy artificial-intelligence computing infrastructure from Broadcom and lease it to Anthropic, and Microsoft offered buyouts to 60,000 employees, roughly 27% of its global workforce, as it spends up to $175 billion on artificial-intelligence infrastructure this year.
business_politics.summary: The Broadcom structure pushes the cost of data center hardware off the balance sheets of the companies that use it and onto banks, Blackstone, and the credit markets, landing the same day Anthropic filed to go public and Meta Platforms disclosed a $95 billion raise. Microsoft is extending the buyouts to workers in the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, and India to hold operating costs down against that capital spending.

business_politics.title: The Justice Department Charges Comey a Third Time
business_politics.latest_developments: Federal prosecutors charged former FBI director James Comey on Monday, October 26, with disclosing national defense information, bypassing a grand jury to bring the case, the same day a federal judge ruled the Trump administration illegally fired the former federal prosecutor Maurene Comey and President Trump offered a $1 million reward for tips leading to an election fraud conviction.
business_politics.summary: This is the third case the Trump administration has brought against Comey, whom Trump fired as FBI director in 2017. The ruling on Maurene Comey's dismissal cuts against the government's claim of sweeping presidential power to remove officials, and the reward offer arrives eight days before a November 3 midterm vote that settles control of Congress.

business_politics.summary: Israelis vote Tuesday, October 27, in a parliamentary election that settles whether Netanyahu keeps the premiership after a run of nearly continuous rule. The Financial Times reports that plans for a renewed assault on Iran survive an electoral defeat for either Netanyahu or President Trump, which keeps Gulf energy supply, tanker traffic, and the Strait of Hormuz exposed whichever way the vote falls.

business_politics.title: Anthropic Files to Go Public as Meta Lines Up $95 Billion
business_politics.latest_developments: Anthropic filed its listing prospectus Monday, October 26, pointing to a November debut, with chief executive Dario Amodei warning in the document of the risk advanced artificial intelligence poses to humanity, and Meta Platforms disclosed a plan to raise up to $95 billion, including a $35 billion stock offering with Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices, and Broadcom as cornerstone investors.
business_politics.summary: Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot, laid out explosive revenue growth alongside steep losses, $800 billion in data center commitments, and a long list of risk factors in a 335-page, 240,000-word filing that could produce the largest stock market debut in history. Meta, the parent of Facebook, is tapping equity and debt to pay for artificial-intelligence data centers and what the company calls personal superintelligence, and both raises land while investors question artificial-intelligence valuations and the credit financing the buildout.

business_politics.title: Lula Wins a Fourth Term and Brazilian Assets Slide
business_politics.latest_developments: Brazil's real suffered its steepest one-day fall since 1999 and the main stock index dropped to a two-month low Monday, October 26, after Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's run-off win, and Flávio Bolsonaro began contesting the result, a challenge that sets up a confrontation between the country's two dominant political camps.
business_politics.summary: Lula, 80, took an unprecedented fourth term as Brazil's president over Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup; the Financial Times calls the result a blow to President Trump's plan for greater United States influence in Latin America. Investors had positioned for a Bolsonaro victory and a tighter budget, and Santander, Spain's largest bank and a heavy earner in Brazil, fell close to 4% as Lula inherits high debt and a congress that moved to the right.

business_politics.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry confirmed the Tehran meetings, which follow Houthi drone and missile attacks on Saudi energy and airport infrastructure and American preparations for strikes on Iran. business.title: The Parental Leave Mandate Heads for a Statewide Fight
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Monday, October 26, that Allegheny County's new paid parental leave mandate has opened a statewide battle over whether Pennsylvania counties may impose such requirements on employers at all.
business.summary: County Executive Sara Innamorato signed the ordinance Thursday, October 22, after an 11-4 Allegheny County Council vote, requiring employers with 15 or more workers to grant 12 weeks of paid parental leave starting in one year, the first county-level mandate of its kind in the country. around_town.title: Shapiro Signs the School Phone Ban

around_town.summary: The law bars Pennsylvania students in all K-12 schools from using cellphones from first bell to last, with exceptions for medical and learning needs, and leaves each district to write its own enforcement policy. around_teams.title: Warren and Dowdle Split the Backfield
around_teams.latest_developments: The Steelers said Monday, October 26, that they feel "really good" about how they are dividing carries between running backs Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle after the win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris.

team_usa.title: What the Americans Take Out of the Gymnastics Worlds
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN published its takeaways Monday, October 26, from the world gymnastics championships in the Netherlands, where China edged the United States women for team gold and the Americans still left with the marquee individual titles.
team_usa.summary: Skye Blakely won the all-around and added bronze on vault and uneven bars, Claire Pease and Reese Esponda went one-two in the floor exercise on the final day, and Fred Richard took the men's floor title. ESPN weighs that depth against the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and the unresolved question of whether Simone Biles competes again.

team_usa.title: The USWNT's Absence From the Ballon d'Or
team_usa.latest_developments: Alexia Putellas of London City Lionesses and Spain won her third women's Ballon d'Or at Monday night's ceremony in London, October 26, with no United States player among the finalists, the subject of an ESPN piece published hours earlier.
team_usa.summary: Americans such as Abby Wambach, Carli Lloyd, and Megan Rapinoe collected world player of the year honors through the 2010s, and the current squad, eight months from the 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil, sends nobody into the final voting as the roster rebuild continues.

sources.title: Will an American woman ever again be the world's best player?

team_usa.title: Pulisic Scores in Milan's Win
team_usa.latest_developments: Christian Pulisic opened the scoring in AC Milan's 2-0 win over Udinese in Serie A on Sunday, October 25, capping what ESPN called a strong day for United States men's national team players in Europe.
team_usa.summary: Pulisic, the captain of the United States men's national team, put Milan ahead as the club recovered from its loss at Bournemouth, and his goal came alongside productive weekends for other American players abroad with the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals against Haiti set for November 14 in Miami and November 17 in Cincinnati, Ohio.

sources.title: Pulisic goal for Milan caps great day for USMNT stars in Europe

team_usa.latest_developments: Croix Bethune of the Kansas City Current recorded her 11th assist of the season Sunday, October 25, a single-season National Women's Soccer League record.
team_usa.summary: Bethune, a United States international midfielder, broke the league mark in her return to form after a season cut short by injury, and her playmaking has driven the Current's attack through the regular season.

reading.author: Stratechery
reading.title: The End of the Internet
reading.summary: Ben Thompson argues that the open internet, where anyone could stand up a server and reach the world, has finally closed, the last step in a consolidation underway for years. He makes the case that what replaces it looks better than the obituaries suggest.

reading.author: Ed Zitron
reading.title: Premium: The Hater's Guide To Blackstone
reading.summary: Zitron dissects Blackstone and the self-mythologizing of founder and chief executive Stephen A. Schwarzman, whose thirty-chapter "My Personal History" series frames him as a man of sensible values. He reads the firm's actual record against that account.

reading.author: Cal Newport
reading.title: The Good Thing About Hard Things
reading.summary: Newport takes up a paper presented at the Conference on Language Modeling, "AI Assistance Reduces Persistence and Hurts Independent Performance," to argue that struggling through difficulty builds the capability that offloading the work erodes.
